lines: Miami, nineteen twenty-five: some lots reportedly sold ten times a day.
Many buyers only paid a binder: a non-refundable deposit.
The rest was due in thirty days. So they flipped it.
January nineteen twenty-six: a sunken ship blocks Miami's harbour.
September nineteen twenty-six: a hurricane hits Miami. Nearly four hundred dead.
In nineteen twenty-six alone, forty Florida banks fail.
The twist? This crash came three years before Wall Street's.
Follow Rich to Ruin for the next crash.
